To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mutations that disrupt salt bridges at the cytoplasm domain interface in Kir channels cause loss of channel activity by inducing a new channel behavior: after removal of inhibitory ATP, Kir channels open but then quickly inactivate.

1) Kir6.2 mutations that disrupt the CD-I induce loss of channel function, 2) the CD-I of Kir6.2 contains a conserved arginine residue, which is essential for channel function, and 3) the CD-I is a key determinant of the inactivating phenotype of Kir6. 2
mutations in Kir6. 2 that disrupt salt bridges at the cytoplasm interface between adjacent subunits cause loss of channel activity due to a novel channel behavior, inactivation.

the molecular basis of disease mutations and channel function.

the molecular basis of channel function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability of CD-I salt bridges is a major determinant in Kir6. 2 and Kir2. 1 channel inactivation and that the stability of intersubunit CD- I salt bridges controls Kir channel inactivation.
the cytoplasm domain interface of adjacent subunits of Kir channels is important for the channel gating.
mutations in Kir6. 2 channels that affect the stability of the cytoplamsic domain interface between subunits can lead to inactivation of the channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytoplasm domain interface of inwardly rectifying potassium channels plays a major role in controlling the channel's gating behavior.
Kir channel gating is controlled in part by interactions between cytoplasmic protein domains.
the cytoplasm domain interface of Kir channels is important for channel gating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Kir6.2 channel activity is regulated by the strength of the interactions between the cytoplasmatic domains of adjacent Kir6.2 monomers.
the stability of a salt bridge at the interface of cytoplasmic (CD) domains of the adjacent subunits is a major determinant for the inactivation process of Kir6.2 channel.
the stability of Kir channel gating can be modulated by the cytoplasmically facing domain interface.
